newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX ends bourse on record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX ends bourse on record closing high.

text.p: Germany's DAX index ended bourse trade on Wednesday at a record closing level having reached an all-time high, boosted by the dollar's ongoing resilience against comments aimed at braking its rise.
The 30-share blue-chip index crossed the 3,220-point hurdle early in the session to hit a record of 3,228.58 points, and ended the session on a lifetime closing high of 3,216.14.

The dollar breached 1.69 marks early on, then fell back after comments by the Bundesbank which said there was no substance to earlier reports that German officials wanted the dollar to trade between 1.70 marks and 1.75 marks.
Over the session the dollar came back, yet again, to stand at 1.6840 marks by the end of floor trade, seemingly impervious to all efforts to halt its advance.
"The market is really rising off the dollar's strength," said one trader.
Export-oriented shares, particularly chemicals, all benefited from the stronger dollar, dealers said.

The chemical sector, long favoured on the German bourse, saw further gains over the session. Bayer AG ended up 1.56 marks at 67.98 marks, Hoechst AG ended up 85 pfennigs at 75.60 marks and BASF ended up 31 pfennigs at 63.35 marks.
German banks were also in favour over the course of floor trade. Commerzbank AG ended up 20 pfennigs at 43.50 marks, Deutsche Bank AG ended 38 pfennigs higher at 84.48 marks.
Dresdner Bank AG ended off earlier highs at 53.40 marks, up seven pfennigs, amid some profit-taking.
